applies_why: The judge breaks challenger link C3 using verses (Matthew 1:18, 1:25, Luke 1:34), and the rule's last sentence brings exactly such link-breaking verses under its quote-and-name counting condition.
quote: D2 vs C3 (Matthew 1:18, 25): CHALLENGER LINK BROKEN -- [L1] Matthew 1:18 "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost" and Matthew 1:25 "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son" contradict C3's claim of espousal union; [L2] πρὶν ἢ συνελθεῖν (prin ē synelthein, Strong's G4250/G4905, before coming together) and οὐκ ἐγίνωσκεν (ouk eginōsken, Strong's G1097, was not knowing); [L3] Luke 1:34.
rule_words: counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way.
room: "A verse the judge uses to break a link is counted this way" — reading one: 'counted this way' extends the 'only when' condition, so a verse may serve to break a link only if the judge also quotes the earlier round's sentence that pressed it against that link and names that round; reading two: the clause merely adds such verses to the unanswered-witness tally and imposes no quote-and-name duty on the act of breaking the link itself.
why: The judge broke C3 with Matthew 1:18, 1:25, and Luke 1:34 while quoting only scripture and Greek forms, never quoting a pressing sentence from any earlier round and naming no round, so it counted as link-breaking witnesses the very verses the rule says do not count without that demonstration.
